shower.thought: We spend our whole lives learning how to be human, but no one ever teaches us, which means we're all just improvising together and pretending we have the manual.
The people who hurt you the most are usually the ones who showed you love first, because they're the only ones who knew exactly where to aim.
You'll never know if you're boring because the people who think so will never tell you, and the people who tell you you're interesting might just be being nice.
Every time you remember something, you're not recalling the original moment—you're recalling the last time you remembered it, like a photocopy of a photocopy getting worse each time.
We fear death but spend most of our lives half-asleep, which means we're practicing dying every single night.
Your name is a sound other people made up before you existed, and you've spent your whole life living up to something you had no say in.
The only time you ever see yourself is in a mirror or a photo, which means you've never actually seen your own face—only a reversed or frozen version of it.
Loneliness is just remembering that you're trapped in a body that no one else can access, no matter how close they get.
We call it "getting over" someone, but really you're just getting used to the absence, which isn't the same thing at all.
If you've ever felt like something major is missing from your life, it might not be a person or a job—it might be that you haven't found what you're supposed to be missing yet.
The most honest conversations you'll ever have are probably with strangers, because they have nothing to lose by telling you the truth.
You can't want what you don't know exists, which means your ideal life might be invisible to you right now.
Every argument you've ever had was really just two people arguing about what the other person meant, not about what they actually said.
We're all walking around with incomplete information about everyone, including ourselves, yet we're confident enough to make huge decisions anyway.
The people who seem the most put-together probably stress about the same weird things you do—they're just better at hiding it.
You've never actually tasted what food "really" tastes like, because your expectations and memories change the flavor before it even hits your tongue.
Nostalgia is just your brain lying to you in a way that feels good, rewriting history into something better than it was.
The scariest part of failure isn't the failure itself—it's the moment you realize you'll have to keep living after it.
You probably know someone who's secretly struggling with something, and they probably think no one cares, and they're probably wrong about that.
If someone remembered every nice thing you ever did for them, you'd think they were obsessed, but if they forget, you think they don't care—there's no winning.

motivational.thought: Progress is measured not by the absence of struggle, but by your willingness to continue despite it. — Unknown
The person you become five years from now will be shaped by the choices you make today. — Unknown
Comfort is the enemy of growth, but growth is the foundation of pride. — Unknown
You can't control the wind, but you can adjust your sails. — Jim Rohn
The only permission you need is the permission you give yourself. — Unknown
Small consistent actions compound into extraordinary results over time. — Unknown
Regret costs more than risk ever will. — Unknown
Your potential is not determined by your circumstances—it's determined by your response to them. — Unknown
The version of yourself that you're avoiding becoming is usually the one you most need to be. — Unknown
Do not wait for the perfect moment; create it. — Unknown
What lies behind you and what lies ahead of you pales in comparison to what lies within you. — Ralph Waldo Emerson
The days you don't feel like working are the days your future self needs you to work. — Unknown
Every expert was once a beginner who refused to stay that way. — Unknown
Your life doesn't improve by chance, it improves by change. — Unknown
The greatest tragedy is not failure—it's the life unlived out of fear of it. — Unknown
Discipline is choosing what you want most over what you want now. — Unknown
You are not behind. You are not late. You are exactly where you need to be. — Unknown
The person who moves a mountain begins by carrying away small stones. — Confucius
Success is the sum of small decisions made consistently. — Unknown
Your doubt is loud, but your potential is louder. — Unknown

darkjoke.thought:
I told my therapist I think I'm a dog.
He said that's fine, just don't bite the other patients. I said, "No promises," and he doubled my copay.

My dad said, "Son, I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed."
I said, "Thanks for the consistency—that's been true since I was born."

I went to a motivational speech about overcoming adversity.
The speaker was incredible until I realized he was just reading my medical history.

My friend said he's cutting everyone toxic out of his life.
I said, "That's great." He said, "Yeah, starting with you." I said, "Finally, something we agree on."

I asked my accountant if I had any money left.
He laughed so hard he had a coughing fit. Then he sent me the bill for the consultation.

My gym trainer said, "No pain, no gain."
I said, "Great news—I'm in constant pain and gaining nothing."

I told my mom I was thinking about my future.
She said, "That's nice." I said, "No, I mean I'm literally just thinking about it, not doing anything."

My date asked what my biggest fear was.
I said, "Commitment." She said, "Mine too," and we've been awkwardly texting ever since.

I said to my boss, "I don't think you appreciate what I do here."
He said, "You're absolutely right. I'll work on that." He's been ignoring me for three weeks.

My therapist asked if I'm self-sabotaging.
I said, "Of course not." Then I immediately proved her point by leaving a one-star review on her office door.

I told my friend he should learn from his mistakes.
He said, "I'm working on it." Three months later, he made the exact same mistake. I said, "Progress?"

My doctor said I have the liver of a 60-year-old.
I said, "That's the nicest thing anyone's ever said to my organs."

I asked my ex why she left me.
She said, "You never listen." I said, "What?" She said, "Exactly."

My mom asked why I never call anymore.
I said, "You always answer." She said, "That's the point!" I said, "Exactly."

I went to my high school reunion.
Everyone was successful except me, which meant I actually won because I set the bar so low.

My landlord said he's raising the rent.
I said, "Can we negotiate?" He said, "Sure, you can negotiate a move-out date."

I told my friend he's being selfish.
He said, "And?" I said, "Nothing, I just wanted you to be aware." He said, "Mission accomplished."

My barber asked how I wanted my hair cut.
I said, "Like I have my life together." He said, "That's impossible, but I'll try."

I asked my coworker if he wanted to grab lunch.
He said, "Can't, I'm busy." He's been "busy" for six months. I'm starting to think it's personal.

My fitness app said I burned 50 calories today.
That's the first honest compliment I've received all year.
